verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a spurious verifier failure: the agent met the instruction to add only regression tests for the reported int32 stack dtype bug, yet SWTBench verified scored reward 0.0 with `resolved: false` [1]. The prompt asked for test cases that verify whether a fix preserves coordinate dtypes through `Dataset.stack`, using only tests and not a source patch [2]. The agent reproduced the MVCE (`int32` becoming `int64` after stack) [3], added a dataset-level assertion mirroring the issue example [4], added a complementary `PandasMultiIndex.stack` level-variable check [5], and ran pytest to confirm both new tests fail on the unfixed codebase (`int64` vs `int32`) [6]. The post-hoc verifier report shows the agent patch was collected and its two new tests became fail-to-pass on gold code (`added_f2p: 2`) while still marking `resolved: false` with zero fix-line coverage (`coverage_pred: 0.0` vs `coverage_gold: 1.0`) [1]; the parser only marks success when `get_resolution_success` returns true, which requires the agent's F2P test-name set to be a strict superset of the hidden reference F2P set and to introduce no regressions [7]. The hidden reference instead adds a separately named parametrized `test_restore_dtype_on_multiindexes` for `int32` and `float32` [8], so the agent's differently named but semantically targeted tests cannot satisfy the name-based superset check even though they discriminate broken from fixed behavior. Against what the agent could know from the instruction alone, it genuinely accomplished the task; the FAIL reflects SWTBench verified's hidden-reference superset gate rather than invalid or missing regression coverage.
